claims.text: Adding graphene nanoplatelets to CoCrFeNi will enable in situ formation of an adaptive tribofilm.
The adaptive tribofilm will provide low friction at room temperature.
The graphene-containing composite will generate a thermally stable protective layer at temperatures up to 800 °C.
Graphene addition will reduce both coefficient of friction and wear rate uniformly from room temperature to 800 °C.
Bulk CoCrFeNi exhibits temperature-dependent tribological degradation under sliding wear.
Approximately 0.5 wt% graphene nanoplatelets is an appropriate low loading for producing the proposed CoCrFeNi composite.
Graphene nanoplatelets can be uniformly dispersed and strategically positioned in CoCrFeNi to promote localized tribofilm formation at the sliding interface.
At low temperatures, the lamellar structure of graphene facilitates shear localization.
At high temperatures, controlled oxidation or structural transformation of graphene forms a dense, passivated tribofilm.
A dense passivated surface layer can suppress continued oxidation and improve high-temperature tribological protection.
The proposed tribofilm will mitigate adhesive wear.
The proposed tribofilm will mitigate oxidative wear.
The graphene-reinforced composite will have lower coefficient of friction than unreinforced CoCrFeNi throughout the full test range.
The graphene-reinforced composite will have lower wear rate than unreinforced CoCrFeNi throughout the full test range.
The base CoCrFeNi alloy shows increased friction and wear rate with temperature variations.
The prediction is scoped to sliding in air from room temperature to 800 °C under controlled load and speed.
The optimum graphene content, dispersion uniformity, tribofilm kinetics, long-term stability, and scalability remain uncertain.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in both friction and wear over the entire temperature range, or failure to observe the adaptive tribofilm, will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The loading is described as a volume fraction in the hypothesis but specified numerically as approximately 0.5 wt% in the intervention; weight fraction and volume fraction are not interchangeable.
